slides.texte_overlay:
Habits that make you
quietly charismatic
Remember what people tell you and bring it up weeks later. "How's your mum's knee?" Nobody expects it. It makes people feel cared for, and they never forget the guy who remembered.
Let others take the spotlight. When someone tells a story, don't top it. Laugh, ask a question, let them shine. People feel great around you, and that's what real charisma is.
Speak a little less than everyone else. When you do talk, make it count. People start leaning in when you open your mouth, because they know it'll be worth hearing.
Be calm when things go wrong. Late train, spilled drink, lost booking. "Okay, no problem, here's what we do." Calm in chaos draws people to you like nothing else.
Give credit freely. "That was Sam's idea, and it was a good one." It costs nothing, it makes people trust you, and it quietly makes you the most respected guy in the room.
Always be learning something. Five minutes a day of history, art or science. Curious people are interesting, and interesting people are quietly charismatic without even trying.
slides.texte_sophia: Before: same stories, same topics, every week. After: five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. Curious people are quietly charismatic without even trying.

slides.texte_overlay: Leave every conversation on a warm note. "Really good catching up, take care." Small, sincere, every time. People remember how you made them feel long after they forget what you said.
